title: Port-Gentil taxi drivers strike over blouse requirement
scope: Local taxi work stoppage; L’Union reports a gathering at Centre social, but timing conflicts with an August 1 onset report and July warning.
organizer: FEGASTA/transport unions are mentioned in context; exact organizer and whether action was renewed are uncertain.

state_target.target: Port-Gentil municipal authorities / governor as reported
state_target.evidence: The dispute concerns municipal blouse requirements and alleged controls; L’Union says governor was asked to decide.

demands_original: Opposition to blouse requirement/cost and alleged controls; L’Union says governor was asked to decide.
participants_original: L’Union reports a gathering at Centre social but supplies no attendance figure.
threshold_50_evidence: A gathering is described, but no count establishes 50 simultaneous participants.

start_date.summary: August 1 Media Time says strike since dawn; L’Union reports launch August 6, so onset is disputed.

end_date.summary: Neither report gives a confirmed end date.

location.summary: Port-Gentil, including a gathering reported at Centre social by L’Union.

scope.summary: Local taxi-driver strike; accounts disagree on start and do not establish continuity from July.

organizer.summary: FEGASTA/affiliated transport unions appear in coverage, but division among drivers is reported and exact call is unclear.

state_target.summary: The dispute concerns municipal blouse requirements and alleged controls; L’Union says governor was asked to decide.

demands.summary: Drivers object to blouse requirement/cost and alleged harassment or extortion.

participants_original.summary: Most affiliated drivers reportedly stopped work and gathered at Centre social; no number is given.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: A gathering is described, but no count establishes 50 simultaneous participants.

state_response.summary: A governor was asked to decide, but no resulting action is established.

notes: Do not merge July 31 and August reports without verified continuity; dates differ.
open_questions: Is August 1 a separate stoppage or one episode with the August 6 strike reported by L’Union?
Did at least 50 people gather simultaneously at Centre social?
When did this action end, and is it continuous with July 31?
Did the governor or municipality take an event-linked decision?

title: Tourism ministry workers sit in over implementation of tourism law and sector governance
location: Libreville, outside/at the Ministry of Tourism
scope: SNAPTOUR-linked sit-in and indefinite strike at the ministry, reported to have ended/suspended after an agreement; no broader national action established.

state_target.target: Ministry of Tourism / state implementation of tourism law
state_target.evidence: Demands concern state implementation of tourism law, public revenue traceability and ministry/agency governance.

demands_original: Application of Law 034/2020, revenue traceability, honoring commitments and AGATOUR governance.
participants_original: A sit-in is reported at the ministry; attendance count is not provided.
threshold_50_evidence: The sit-in is described without a participant count; 50 simultaneous participants are not established.

start_date.summary: September reports place the sit-in/indefinite strike onset on August 28.

end_date.summary: La Une reports suspension after a September 18 agreement.

location.summary: Tourism ministry in Libreville; reports describe a sit-in at ministry premises.

scope.summary: SNAPTOUR-led ministry-worker action; no broader national or multi-location event established.

state_target.summary: Demands concern state implementation of tourism law, public revenue traceability and ministry/agency governance.

demands.summary: Apply Law 034/2020, account for sector revenues, honor commitments and address AGATOUR governance.

participants_original.summary: Sit-in reported, but no attendance figure.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The sit-in is described without a participant count; 50 simultaneous participants are not established.

state_response.summary: La Une reports a ministerial agreement on September 18 and union suspension/return to work; implementation is not evidenced.

notes: Agreement supports accommodation only as dialogue/settlement and suspension; do not infer implementation. Cross-month sources were opened in September.
open_questions: Did the sit-in include at least 50 simultaneous participants?
What elements of the agreement were implemented, and over what period?
Were the Gabonclic and Gabonactu reports independently sourced?
